notes.summary:
In the active voice the subject does the action: Ravi wrote a letter. In the passive voice the receiver of the action becomes the subject: A letter was written by Ravi.

SSC gives one sentence and asks for its passive (sometimes its active) form. You get 1 to 2 questions in Tier 1 and a few more in Tier 2. Almost every wrong option changes the tense, breaks agreement (is/are, was/were), uses being or been in the wrong place, or forgets to keep a question as a question. If you know the tense table below, most questions take under 30 seconds.

concepts.title: The five-step method
concepts.body:
1. Find the verb and its tense. Underline the main verb and its helpers (is writing, had seen, will be sent).
  2. Find the object. Only verbs with an object (transitive verbs) can become passive. He sleeps has no passive.
  3. Make the object the new subject. Change pronoun case: me → I, us → we, him → he, her → she, them → they.
  4. Write the verb as a form of be + past participle (V3). The form of be carries the original tense and agrees with the new subject.
  5. Add by + the old subject in object case (I → me, he → him, they → them). Drop it if the doer is unknown or obvious (someone, people, they in a general sense).

Example: She is cleaning the rooms. → present continuous, plural new subject → The rooms are being cleaned by her.

concepts.title: Full tense table
concepts.body:
TenseActivePassive
Simple presentHe writes a letter.A letter is written by him.
Present continuousHe is writing a letter.A letter is being written by him.
Present perfectHe has written a letter.A letter has been written by him.
Simple pastHe wrote a letter.A letter was written by him.
Past continuousHe was writing a letter.A letter was being written by him.
Past perfectHe had written a letter.A letter had been written by him.
Simple futureHe will write a letter.A letter will be written by him.
Future perfectHe will have written a letter.A letter will have been written by him.
Going toHe is going to write a letter.A letter is going to be written by him.
ModalsHe can / must / should write a letter.A letter can / must / should be written by him.
Perfect modalsHe should have written a letter.A letter should have been written by him.

No usual passive: present perfect continuous, past perfect continuous, future continuous and future perfect continuous. If an option gives has been being written, it is wrong.

concepts.title: Being, been and be
concepts.body:
Most traps are about these three words. Learn one line each:

  • being appears only in continuous passives: is being repaired, was being repaired.
  • been appears only in perfect passives: has been repaired, had been repaired, will have been repaired.
  • be (plain form) comes after will, shall and every modal: will be repaired, must be repaired, ought to be repaired.
CorrectIncorrect
The road is being widened.The road is been widened.
The work has been finished.The work has being finished.
The form must be signed.The form must been signed.
A market was being operated.A market was been operated.

concepts.title: Agreement, pronouns and the agent
concepts.body:
• The new subject decides the helper: The plants are watered (plural), The plant is watered (singular). Do not copy the number of the old subject.
  • Pronoun case changes both ways. Active subject they becomes by them; active object him becomes subject he.
    Correct: He was helped by us. Incorrect: Him was helped by we.
  • Drop the agent when it adds nothing: Someone has stolen my bag. → My bag has been stolen. (not by someone). People speak English all over the world. → English is spoken all over the world.
  • Words like every morning, yesterday, already, never stay in the passive sentence, usually in the same position: The sailors had never encountered such a rough sea. → Such a rough sea had never been encountered by the sailors.
  • Only the clause with the object changes. In The committee was reviewing the proposal when the chairman arrived, the clause the chairman arrived stays as it is (arrive has no object).

concepts.title: Negatives and questions
concepts.body:
Negatives: not goes after the first helper.

  • She does not like tea. → Tea is not liked by her. (do/does/did disappear in the passive)
  • They did not invite me. → I was not invited by them.
  • Nobody saw him. → He was not seen by anybody. (nobody becomes not ... by anybody)

Yes/no questions: start with the helper of the passive.

  • Do you know him? → Is he known to you?
  • Did you hear that noise? → Was that noise heard by you?
  • Have they finished the work? → Has the work been finished by them?
  • Can you solve this sum? → Can this sum be solved by you?

Wh-questions: keep the question word.

ActivePassive
Who wrote this letter?By whom was this letter written?
Whom did you invite?Who was invited by you?
What are you doing?What is being done by you?
Why did he beat the dog?Why was the dog beaten by him?
When will you finish the job?When will the job be finished by you?

A passive question must still end with a question mark and keep question order (helper before subject). By whom you were invited? is wrong; By whom were you invited? is right.

concepts.title: Commands and requests (imperatives)
concepts.body:
Two accepted patterns:

  1. Let + object + be + V3: Shut the door. → Let the door be shut.
  2. You are + requested / ordered / advised / forbidden + to + V1, chosen by the tone:
    • Request (please, kindly): Please help me. → You are requested to help me.
    • Order: Leave the room. → You are ordered to leave the room.
    • Advice: Work hard. → You are advised to work hard.

Negative commands:

  • Do not touch the wire. → Let the wire not be touched. or You are warned not to touch the wire.
  • Don't tell lies. → Let lies not be told.

Sentences that already start with Let: Let him do the work. → Let the work be done by him.

Without an object, use the second pattern: Go there. → You are ordered to go there.

concepts.title: Verbs with two objects
concepts.body:
Verbs like give, send, offer, show, teach, tell, lend, pay, promise, award, ask, bring take a person (indirect object) and a thing (direct object). Either can become the subject.

ActivePassive (person first)Passive (thing first)
She gave me a pen.I was given a pen by her.A pen was given to me by her.
The teacher taught us grammar.We were taught grammar by the teacher.Grammar was taught to us by the teacher.
They have offered him a job.He has been offered a job.A job has been offered to him.
The jury awarded her the prize.She was awarded the prize by the jury.The prize was awarded to her by the jury.

When the thing comes first, add to (or for with buy, make, get) before the person. Both forms are correct; SSC options usually contain only one of them.

concepts.title: Infinitives, gerunds and prepositional verbs
concepts.body:
• Infinitive object: I want you to write a letter. → I want a letter to be written by you.
  • Need / deserve + -ing already has a passive meaning: The car needs washing = The car needs to be washed.
  • Gerund: She hates people laughing at her. → She hates being laughed at.
  • Prepositional and phrasal verbs keep their particle, so two prepositions can sit together: They laughed at the beggar. → The beggar was laughed at by them. She looks after the child. → The child is looked after by her. They put off the meeting. → The meeting was put off.
  • Reporting verbs (say, believe, know, think): People say that he is honest. → It is said that he is honest. or He is said to be honest.
  • Make, help, see, hear + bare infinitive take to in the passive: They made him work. → He was made to work. I saw her dance. → She was seen to dance.

concepts.title: Agents that do not take by
concepts.body:
Some past participles behave like adjectives and take a fixed preposition instead of by:

ActivePassive
I know him.He is known to me.
His work pleased me.I was pleased with his work.
The news surprised us.We were surprised at the news.
Water filled the tank.The tank was filled with water.
Music interests her.She is interested in music.
The result disappointed him.He was disappointed with / at the result.
Snow covered the hills.The hills were covered with snow.

concepts.title: Passive to active
concepts.body:
1. Find the doer after by. It becomes the subject (change case: by him → he).
  2. Read the tense from the passive helper: is written → simple present, was being written → past continuous, will have been written → future perfect.
  3. Write the active verb in that tense, agreeing with the new subject.
  • The thief was caught by the police. → The police caught the thief.
  • English is taught by Mr Rao. → Mr Rao teaches English.
  • Let the gate be opened. → Open the gate.
  • By whom were you taught English? → Who taught you English?
  • My request should be considered. (no agent) → You should consider my request. or They should consider my request. Choose the option that keeps the modal.

concepts.title: Sentences that cannot be made passive
concepts.body:
• Intransitive verbs (no object): die, arrive, sleep, go, come, happen, laugh, rise, exist. The baby slept. has no passive.
  • Linking verbs: He became a doctor. She seems tired.
  • Some state verbs with have, resemble, fit, lack: She has a car. is not changed to A car is had by her. He resembles his father. has no passive.

If the given sentence has two clauses, change only the clause with a transitive verb, and leave the other clause untouched.

varieties.name: Simple present
varieties.how: Active V1/V1+s becomes is/am/are + V3. do/does in negatives and questions disappear.

example.q: Select the passive form: The gardener waters the plants every morning.
steps: waters is simple present.
New subject the plants is plural, so use are.
are + watered, agent by the gardener, time phrase stays.
example.answer: The plants are watered by the gardener every morning.

varieties.name: Simple past
varieties.how: Active V2 becomes was/were + V3. Going back, was/were + V3 becomes V2.

example.q: Select the passive form: Marvel Comics created Superman.
steps: created is simple past.
New subject Superman is singular, so use was.
was created by Marvel Comics.
example.answer: Superman was created by Marvel Comics.

varieties.name: Future tenses
varieties.how: Simple future: will/shall + be + V3. Future perfect: will/shall + have been + V3. will never changes with number.

example.q: Select the passive form: By next June, they will have built the new flyover.
steps: will have built is future perfect.
Pattern: will have been + V3.
Agent by them can stay or be dropped; options keep it.
example.answer: By next June, the new flyover will have been built by them.

varieties.name: Present continuous
varieties.how: is/am/are + being + V3. Look for being; an option with been is wrong.

example.q: Select the passive form: The workers are repairing the bridge.
steps: are repairing is present continuous.
New subject the bridge is singular, so use is being.
is being repaired by the workers.
example.answer: The bridge is being repaired by the workers.

varieties.name: Past continuous
varieties.how: was/were + being + V3. Change only the clause that has an object.

example.q: Select the passive form: The committee was reviewing the proposal when the chairman arrived.
steps: Main clause was reviewing is past continuous.
The proposal was being reviewed by the committee.
arrived has no object, so that clause stays as it is.
example.answer: The proposal was being reviewed by the committee when the chairman arrived.

varieties.name: Present perfect
varieties.how: has/have + been + V3, with has or have chosen by the new subject.

example.q: Select the passive form: They have completed the new library building.
steps: have completed is present perfect.
New subject the building is singular, so has been.
Agent by them.
example.answer: The new library building has been completed by them.

varieties.name: Past perfect
varieties.how: had + been + V3 for every subject. Adverbs like never, already stay between had and been.

example.q: Select the passive form: The sailors had never encountered such a rough sea.
steps: had encountered is past perfect.
Pattern: had been + V3, with never after had.
New subject such a rough sea, agent by the sailors.
example.answer: Such a rough sea had never been encountered by the sailors.

varieties.name: Modal verbs
varieties.how: modal + be + V3; perfect modals become modal + have been + V3. Keep the same modal.

example.q: Select the passive form: We can buy books online.
steps: Modal can + buy.
Pattern: can be + V3, so can be bought.
by us is obvious and is usually dropped.

varieties.name: Verbs with two objects
varieties.how: Either object can lead. Person first: I was given a pen. Thing first: add to: A pen was given to me.

example.q: Select the passive form: The principal awarded Meena a gold medal.
steps: awarded is simple past with two objects: Meena (person) and a gold medal (thing).
Person first: Meena was awarded a gold medal by the principal.
Thing first would be A gold medal was awarded to Meena by the principal; both are correct, pick the one in the options.
example.answer: Meena was awarded a gold medal by the principal.

varieties.name: Commands and requests
varieties.how: Let + object + be + V3, or You are requested / ordered / advised + to + V1 by tone. Negative: Let ... not be + V3.

example.q: Select the passive form: Please submit the form by Friday.
steps: It is a polite request (please).
Pattern: You are requested to + V1.
Let the form be submitted is also possible, but it loses the politeness; prefer the request form when please is present.
example.answer: You are requested to submit the form by Friday.

varieties.name: Questions
varieties.how: Keep it a question. Yes/no: start with the passive helper (Was the noise heard...?). Who becomes By whom; whom becomes who.

example.q: Select the passive form: Did you hear that noise?
steps: Did + hear is simple past, so the helper is was.
Question order: Was + that noise + heard.
Agent by you and the question mark stay.
example.answer: Was that noise heard by you?

varieties.name: Special structures
varieties.how: Keep particles (laughed at), add to after made/seen, use It is said that for reporting verbs, and use known to, pleased with instead of by.

example.q: Select the passive form: The children laughed at the joker.
steps: laugh at is a prepositional verb; at stays with the verb.
Simple past: was laughed at.
Then by the children, so at by appear together, which is correct.
example.answer: The joker was laughed at by the children.

tips: Name the tense first. Then strike out every option whose helper shows a different tense; usually two options go at once.
Look at the new subject before choosing is/are or was/were. The number of the old subject does not matter.
If a question is given, the answer must also be a question with a question mark.
With please or kindly, prefer 'You are requested to ...'; with a plain command, 'Let ... be + V3' is the safe choice.
Drop 'by someone', 'by people' and 'by us' when the doer is general; SSC answers usually drop them.
For passive to active, the word after 'by' becomes the subject. If there is no 'by', use a sensible subject (they, you, someone) and keep the same tense.
Time words (yesterday, every day, already) never change. An option that changes them is wrong.
traps: Being belongs only to continuous tenses and been only to perfect tenses. 'Is been written' and 'has being written' are always wrong.
Do not change the tense: 'They have completed' becomes 'has been completed', not 'was completed'.
Who becomes 'By whom', not 'Whom by' or 'By who'. 'Whom did you call?' becomes 'Who was called by you?'
Prepositional verbs keep their preposition: 'The child was looked after', not 'The child was looked'.
After make, see, hear and help, the passive needs 'to': 'He was made to work', not 'He was made work'.
Some sentences have no passive (die, arrive, sleep, become, resemble). If only one clause has an object, change only that clause.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
The gardener waters the plants every morning.
options: The plants are watered by the gardener every morning.
The plants were watered by the gardener every morning.
The plants are being watered by the gardener every morning.
The plants have been watered by the gardener every morning.
questions.solution: Simple present → are + V3 (plural subject plants). So: The plants are watered by the gardener every morning.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.
The match was won by our team.
options: Our team wins the match.
Our team has won the match.
Our team won the match.
Our team had won the match.
questions.solution: was won is simple past passive. The active form keeps the simple past: Our team won the match.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
They have completed the new library building.
options: The new library building was completed by them.
The new library building has been completed by them.
The new library building had been completed by them.
The new library building is being completed by them.
questions.solution: Present perfect → has/have been + V3. Subject building is singular: has been completed by them.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
Switch off the lights before leaving.
options: The lights are switched off before leaving.
Let the lights switch off before leaving.
Let the lights be switched off before leaving.
The lights should switch off before leaving.
questions.solution: An imperative becomes Let + object + be + V3: Let the lights be switched off before leaving.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
Who invited you to the party?
options: By whom were you invited to the party?
Who were you invited by the party?
By whom you were invited to the party?
Whom has invited you to the party?
questions.solution: Who becomes By whom; simple past passive in question order is were you invited. So: By whom were you invited to the party?

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
The committee was reviewing the proposal when the chairman arrived.
options: The proposal had been reviewed by the committee when the chairman arrived.
The proposal was reviewed by the committee when the chairman was arrived.
The proposal was being reviewed by the committee when the chairman arrived.
The proposal is being reviewed by the committee when the chairman arrived.
questions.solution: Only the main clause changes. Past continuous → was/were being + V3: was being reviewed. arrived is intransitive and stays unchanged.

flashcards.front: Passive of a modal (can, must, should)
flashcards.back: modal + be + V3: can be done, must be finished

flashcards.front: Prepositions after known, pleased, surprised, filled (passive)
Which tenses have no usual passive?
flashcards.back: All perfect continuous tenses and future continuous. Intransitive verbs (die, go, sleep, arrive) have no passive at all.
